name: Orto Botanico di Lucca
title: Ancient Trees in Lucca's Botanical Garden: 7 to Find
meta_description: Lucca's 1820 teaching garden: a cedar planted the same year as a Corsican pine, a lightning-split ginkgo, and a Balearic box grown to full size.
intro: Lucca's botanical garden was founded in 1820 by Maria Luisa di Borbone, Duchess of Lucca, and its early directors recorded exact planting dates for several of these trees. A cedar of Lebanon and a Corsican pine went in together in 1822; a redwood arrived around 1850, one of the first raised in Europe; a ginkgo, felled by lightning, regrew as three trunks from one root. By the pond, a pair of bald cypresses throw up woody knees from the water and turn rust orange each autumn, the garden's only conifer that behaves like a deciduous tree. Nearby, a seven-metre Balearic box grows to a size the species rarely reaches outside its native islands, next to the garden's youngest registered tree, a silver lime planted around 1900, and a fastigiate yew whose thickness belies how slowly the species grows. The garden charges standard admission.
